gap: No result ChatGPT got states, side by side, which under-$50 Hall effect boards work without a cable and which accept other makers' magnetic switches: the Gamakay NS68 is sold in a Tri-mode version ($39.99) and takes 3-pin magnetic switches from Gateron or TTC (TechX Reviews), the Epomaker HE68 Lite is USB only, and Redragon's K617 HE switches fit no other brand's.
standout_why: Compared against hlplanet.com (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net's HE68 Lite review (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net's budget guide, chronicreload.com, deal.ai and setupinsider.com; pcgamer.com (cited) returned only navigation, so it was not compared. Each already holds one cell: hlplanet says the NS68 is 'wired or wireless' and the cheapest wireless option, at a stale $42.99; mechanicalkeyboard.net says the HE68 Lite is wired only and magnetic-only hot-swap; chronicreload says the K617 HE's switches are Redragon-only and the WIN68 HE driver is Windows-only. None gives polling rate per connection mode for any board, none names which third-party switches fit the NS68, and none puts the picks in one matrix. The cell that would have lifted this to 2 or 3, the NS68 Tri-mode's polling rate on 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth from Gamakay's own page, could not be read: gamakay.com product pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt.
decides: It confirms a segment rather than changing the overall pick. A shopper who wants a Hall effect board under $50 without a cable has one sourced option here, the Gamakay NS68 Tri-mode at $39.99, a partner-store product we can link. It does not displace the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro ($37.40 on MCHOSE's store today) or the Epomaker HE68 Lite ($42.49) for wired play. The page should not claim 8,000 Hz for the NS68's wireless modes: only the wired figure is sourced.
